item.title: Researchers propose quantum Earth observation for photon-limited environments
item.description: Have you ever wondered what Earth observation satellites see when they look down at the deep ocean or a dense tropical forest during the dead of night? The answer, for the most part, is nothing. Standard optical sensors require a steady stream of light to function, and in these photon-limited regions, they hit a hard physical boundary. But what if we could rewrite the rules of optical imaging? By borrowing techniques from quantum photonics, we can push beyond these classical limits and unlock a fundamentally new way to observe the darkest and most hidden environments on our planet. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Structural study explains how cells stabilize protective membrane pockets
item.description: Our cells' membranes have many functions. They not only provide mechanical protection but also precisely control which substances enter or leave cells. Among other functions, they protect blood vessel cells, which are frequently exposed to strong mechanical forces. In addition, caveolae serve as signaling centers that help regulate blood pressure. item.title: Economists examine how people infer, revise beliefs in face of new information
item.description: When people hear something new about a topic, they should update their beliefs to reflect the new information. item.title: A painting signed 'L daVinci': Analysis reveals Renaissance pigments and later alterations
item.description: Researchers at Uppsala University have analyzed the color pigments in a historical painting signed "L daVinci." item.description: A new 3D structure of a cancer-linked protein bound to its cellular partner reveals details of how the protein binds to chromosomes and could offer insights for future disease treatments.
